citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not currently have a written program of veterinary care for the llamas, goat, or alpacas maintained at the
facility. The written program of veterinary care is needed to ensure that the facility understands the expectations of the
attending veterinarian regarding the veterinary care of the regulated animals, affirming that both parties have a clear
understanding of their roles to appropriately manage the species on hand.
In coordination with the attending veterinarian, the facility must establish and document a written program of veterinary
care for the animals at the facility. The facility should ensure that the written program of veterinary care is available for
review during all USDA inspections, with the documented arrangements to include regularly scheduled visits to the
premises of the facility.
Correct by July 25, 2026.

The enclosures housing the goat and llamas have fencing that is in disrepair. Multiple gaps are present under the
enclosure fencing and shelter walls due to erosion and movement of dirt. The resulting gaps between the ground and
fence vary in size and are approximately 6-10 inches in diameter. The fencing between the female and male llama
enclosures also has a hole in the wire mesh that is approximately 12-18 inches in diameter with the wire unraveling
resulting in sharp wire points present at the edges of the hole.
Compromised structural integrity within primary enclosures can provide an opportunity for entrapment or injury to the
animals contained therein. Outdoor housing facilities shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to
protect the animals from injury and to contain the animals.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
